title: Choose the new look for 3D Print OS
question: Four modern directions for the staff console, each sketched as the dashboard. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Facts Panel
options.thesis: Airy white console where every job and quote carries its numbers as a crisp facts panel: time, grams, layers, price.
materials: thick-thin rule ladder only inside facts panels
options.viewport: Light rail, a greeting with four figures and a revenue sparkline, a printer grid where each card shows its current job as a mini facts panel, and a needs-a-hand list on the right.
options.risk: Calm and clean can drift toward generic SaaS if the facts panels are set timidly.

raised.raise: Neutrals snap to one nine-step cool grey ramp; no stray greys.
Cobalt is reserved for 'printing now' and appears nowhere else.
The dashboard reflows by whole grid cells; no odd-width cards.
One face carries headings, figures and labels; ink is never pure black.

options.label: Parcel Tracker
options.thesis: Every order is a tracked parcel: a stage line from quoted to delivered, so staff and customers read progress the same way.
options.viewport: Top figures, a fleet row of printer cards, and an order list where each row carries its stage line with the current stage in teal.
options.risk: Familiar: it is the look delivery apps and many modern consoles already ship.

options.label: Next-Up Signage
options.thesis: Each printer is a gate: big printer number, and one yellow band that says only the next thing to do there.
options.viewport: Printers as gate panels across the top with their next action on a yellow band, then quotes and orders below on a calm white ground.
options.case: Wins on clarity at the printer (next step readable from a metre away); loses on how much it says about pricing and quotes.
options.risk: Yellow must stay reserved for next actions or it turns loud fast.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: An order is a coupon book: quote, payment, print, QC and delivery tear off in sequence, and cancelled ones stamp VOID instead of vanishing.
options.viewport: Printer column of job coupons with stub numbers, and a quotes table where each row ends in its coupon stage.
options.case: Holds product clarity (order stages map to coupons); audience ties to print shops are weaker.
options.risk: Perforations and stamps become costume if overused.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over a backlit zone ramp.
options.case: Shop staff do not identify with darkroom work and the hatching hides status.
options.risk: Dark and cryptic for floor use.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain colours below, the active course in purple above.
options.viewport: Printers as terrain, jobs as a course.
options.case: The map metaphor makes a queue harder to read, not easier.
options.kept: One colour reserved for what is active right now.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.case: Poster type fights a working table.
options.risk: Reads as a poster, not a tool.
options.kept: Layout reflows by whole grid cells.

options.label: Design Annual
options.thesis: Near-white stock, registration marks, one grotesque.
options.viewport: Printers as plates in a 4-up row.
options.case: Editorial calm without the status colour the floor needs.
options.kept: One face for everything; ink never pure black.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern SaaS admin, like Linear or Vercel, done carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, four stat tiles, a printer status table and a recent quotes table.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other admin by design.
